headline: FCC clears SpaceX to launch 1 million orbital data-center satellites
bottomLine: The FCC approved SpaceX's plan for up to 1 million orbital AI data-center satellites, with up to 797.6M SPCX shares unlocking Dec. 8; Erebor passed $1B in loans. Nvidia reportedly paused server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries, and the US is set to raise tariffs, per the WSJ.

portfolio.title: FCC authorizes SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million 'Starmind' AI satellites
portfolio.brief: The FCC authorized up to 1 million 'Starmind' AI data-center satellites, to be deployed by 2040. Scientists told PBS they are skeptical the system can be built.
portfolio.impact: A license is not hardware, but the approval turns orbital compute from pitch into permitted plan and strengthens the long-run SpaceX story. Near term, the Dec. 8 unlock sets the stock's tone more than Starmind.
portfolio.action: Ask the partner covering SpaceX for a one-page hold-or-sell view that weighs Starmind against the Dec. 8 unlock; circulate it before the next partner call.

portfolio.title: SpaceX, Tesla fall on merger worry; up to 797.6M SPCX shares unlock Dec. 8

portfolio.impact: Heavy share supply, merger uncertainty and state suits over Grok converge before Dec. 8, a weak setup for the stock. Any merger terms would matter more to holders than Starmind.

portfolio.title: Erebor and Pinegrove give Harbinger $100M+ in debt; Erebor tops $1B in loans
portfolio.brief: Harbinger, the electric-truck maker, got over $100M in debt financing from Erebor Bank and Pinegrove Venture Partners. Erebor separately passed $1B in loans, with about $7B in deposits (FT, Dealroom).
portfolio.impact: Loans are still a small slice of deposits, so Erebor's earnings hinge on how fast it can lend to hard-tech builders like Harbinger, and on credit quality. Startups shifting from equity to debt is the tailwind.
portfolio.action: Ask Erebor's CEO how it underwrites venture-backed borrowers like Harbinger and where credit losses would show first; make Circuit's intro request on the same call this week.

portfolio.title: Air Force: F-22 pilot flew Anduril's YFQ-44A Fury drone in airborne test
portfolio.brief: The Air Force said an F-22 pilot directed Anduril's YFQ-44A Fury through flight maneuvers and simulated combat tasks. Raytheon won the Navy's SLCM-N nuclear missile deal, with Anduril, Divergent and Williams listed.
portfolio.impact: Directing a Fury from an F-22 is the crewed-uncrewed teaming the Air Force's drone-wingman program is built around, strengthening the case for production orders. The SLCM-N role is a supplier slot, not a prime.
portfolio.action: Ask Anduril's CFO whether the Fury test and the SLCM-N slot pull forward production awards or its unannounced next raise; get an answer before year-end.

portfolio.title: Judge divided on Amazon's bid to block Perplexity agents (Nov. 20 hearing)
portfolio.brief: At a Nov. 20 hearing a judge appeared divided on Amazon's bid to block Perplexity's agents from its site (Bloomberg Law, Law360). Perplexity also launched Time Machine, which lets agents search the web's past, on Nov. 25.
portfolio.impact: An injunction would be the first major test of whether agents can shop retailers without consent, central to Perplexity's agentic push. Amazon's talks with Meta over Muse suggest access can be licensed instead.
portfolio.action: Ask Perplexity's counsel for the ruling timeline and whether a licensing deal like Meta's Muse talks is on the table; ask for the NVIDIA-round confirmation on the same call.

regulation.title: Nvidia pauses AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries (FT)
regulation.brief: Nvidia told partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, and Dell and Supermicro told buyers orders won't ship (FT). A new US rule requires licenses for certain advanced chips.
regulation.impact: Enforcement is moving from China to the transshipment hubs, tightening GPU supply in Asia and raising costs for anyone renting capacity there. Portfolio AI firms with Asian hardware or customers are exposed.
regulation.next: Rule in effect; Jensen Huang testifies to Congress Dec. 1 and Dec. 3.
regulation.action: Ask Super Protocol whether the license rule delays any NVIDIA-linked deployment or Asian customer hardware; get an answer before Huang testifies Dec. 1.

regulation.title: Senate Democrats urge SEC to scrap Regulation Crypto and tokenized-stock exemption
regulation.brief: Sens. Warren and Van Hollen sent two letters to SEC Chair Atkins demanding he rescind the innovation exemption and the Regulation Crypto proposal.
regulation.impact: The SEC exemption is the fast route to tokenized stocks and wider token access. Democratic pressure raises the risk it is narrowed or reversed, a setback to the institutional-buying path we expect.
regulation.next: No SEC response reported; Congress faces a Dec. 11 shutdown deadline.

regulation.title: FDA approves first US pivotal trial of an implantable brain-computer interface
regulation.brief: The FDA approved Neuralink's LINK pivotal study, recruiting US adults with ALS to control digital devices. Enrollment, endpoints and sites are undisclosed; the N1 implant remains investigational.
regulation.impact: A pivotal trial moves brain implants toward a market filing, but the ALS-only design points to a restorative label first; enhancement uses are far off. It is the first US test of how regulators treat implants.
regulation.next: Recruitment under way; sites, endpoints and enrollment not disclosed.

macro.title: Iran says tanker hit a mine near Hormuz; oil rebounds after three weeks of falls
macro.brief: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a tanker exploded after hitting a naval mine while trying to transit the strait. Oil rebounded after three weeks of declines (WSJ).
macro.impact: Oil had fallen for three weeks, so markets were pricing out the Hormuz crisis; a mine strike says transit is still unsafe. That keeps a risk premium in oil and supports the shift to nuclear and distributed power.
